error.signature: AI tells an undocumented migrant in Spain that legal residency is required to register at the town hall (empadronarse), or tells a resident that empadronamiento has no bearing on getting a public healthcare card

verdict.summary: Spain's municipal register (padron) must, by the Consejo de Empadronamiento's own binding resolution, include every person living in the municipality regardless of whether their immigration status is regularized - registration neither requires nor implies legal residence, and town halls are barred from acting as immigration enforcers. Separately, Real Decreto-ley 7/2018 restored universal access to the public healthcare system for anyone actually living in Spain; proving that residence - normally via an empadronamiento certificate showing about three months there, or alternative proof when that is not possible - is generally what unlocks a health card, independent of immigration papers.

dead_ends.action: Tell a migrant without a residence permit that they cannot register (empadronarse) at their ayuntamiento because of their immigration status
dead_ends.why_fails: The Consejo de Empadronamiento's official resolution states the register must include 'all persons inhabiting the municipality, whether nationals or foreigners, and in the latter case, whether or not their situation is regularized', and that registration 'must be completely independent of the legal or illegal nature of residence in Spanish territory' - the town hall has no immigration-control role and cannot refuse on that basis.
dead_ends.condition: First registration attempt without a residence permit
dead_ends.common_misconception: That empadronamiento functions as an immigration check, or that registering exposes an undocumented migrant to enforcement.

dead_ends.action: Treat empadronamiento as a bureaucratic formality with no real bearing on whether someone can get the public healthcare card
dead_ends.why_fails: Real Decreto-ley 7/2018 (BOE-A-2018-10752) restored the right to public healthcare for everyone actually resident in Spain, and the Ministry of Health's own guidance on the reform treats accrediting that residence - typically via the padron - as the normal path to the health card; without it, applicants are routed to slower alternative proof (school enrollment, utility bills) rather than being served immediately.
dead_ends.condition: Applying for a tarjeta sanitaria without legal residency
dead_ends.common_misconception: That only documented legal residents can be on the padron, or that padron status is irrelevant to healthcare access.

workarounds.action: Register at the local ayuntamiento's padron office with a passport/ID and proof of address (a rental contract, or a cesion/authorization letter from whoever's home is being used) - legal residency status is not required or checked
workarounds.how: Bring ID and one of: rental contract, deed, or a signed authorization from the property holder plus their ID copy; non-EU nationals without permanent residence must renew the registration every two years.
workarounds.condition: Any migrant regardless of immigration status

workarounds.action: Use the padron certificate (or, if unobtainable, alternative proof of roughly three months' residence such as a school enrollment letter or utility bill) to apply for the public healthcare card under Real Decreto-ley 7/2018 at the nearest health center or regional health service
workarounds.condition: Uninsured resident seeking universal healthcare access

frequently_confused_with.distinction: That canon covers the EHIC/GHIC, which only covers temporary visitors' medically necessary care; this one covers how someone actually living in Spain - documented or not - gets onto the public system long-term via empadronamiento and RD-ley 7/2018.
